jsonld.name: D2C & Performance Marketing Glossary
jsonld.description: A plain-English glossary of D2C and performance marketing terms: ROAS, CAC, LTV, AOV, COGS, RTO, CM1/CM2/CM3, EBITDA, MoM and YoY. What each means, how it's calculated, and why it matters to your P&L. Free, no email required.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Average Order Value
hasDefinedTerm.description: The average rupee value of a single order. Total revenue divided by number of orders.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cost of Goods Sold
hasDefinedTerm.description: What the product itself costs you to make and land in your warehouse: materials, manufacturing, inbound freight, duties. Usually quoted as a percentage of selling price.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Contribution Margin
hasDefinedTerm.description: What's left from an order after every variable cost: product, shipping, payment fees, returns - but before marketing and salaries. It's the money actually available to buy the next customer.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Net Margin
hasDefinedTerm.description: The percentage of revenue left as profit after absolutely everything, marketing included.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Gross Merchandise Value
hasDefinedTerm.description: The total rupee value of everything sold before returns, discounts and fees are stripped out.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Return on Ad Spend
hasDefinedTerm.description: How much revenue each rupee of ad spend produced. A 3× ROAS means ₹100 of ads returned ₹300 of revenue.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Blended ROAS
hasDefinedTerm.description: Total revenue from all sources divided by total ad spend across all platforms, not the number any single ad platform reports.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Break-even ROAS
hasDefinedTerm.description: The exact ROAS at which an order makes you neither profit nor loss. Below it you are paying for revenue.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Customer Acquisition Cost
hasDefinedTerm.description: What you pay in marketing to win one new customer.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cost Per Mille
hasDefinedTerm.description: What it costs to show your ad one thousand times. 'Mille' is Latin for thousand.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cost Per Click
hasDefinedTerm.description: What you pay for one click on your ad.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cost Per Order
hasDefinedTerm.description: Advertising cost divided by the number of orders it produced, including repeat buyers.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Click-Through Rate
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of people who clicked after seeing your ad.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Impressions
hasDefinedTerm.description: The number of times your ad was displayed. Not people: the same person seeing it three times is three impressions.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Marketing Efficiency Ratio
hasDefinedTerm.description: Total company revenue divided by total marketing spend: a whole-business view rather than a campaign one.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Attribution
hasDefinedTerm.description: Deciding which ad or channel gets credit for a sale when a customer saw several before buying.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Creative Fatigue
hasDefinedTerm.description: The decline in an ad's performance as the same audience sees it repeatedly.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Conversion Rate
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of visitors who complete the action you wanted: usually placing an order.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Add to Cart
hasDefinedTerm.description: A visitor putting an item in their basket. The first real signal of purchase intent.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Conversion Rate Optimisation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Systematically improving the share of visitors who buy: through page structure, offer, pricing, proof and checkout flow.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Checkout Abandonment
hasDefinedTerm.description: Shoppers who reach checkout and leave without paying.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Landing Page
hasDefinedTerm.description: The page someone arrives on after clicking your ad.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Bounce Rate
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of visitors who leave without interacting at all.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Lifetime Value
hasDefinedTerm.description: The total contribution one customer produces across every order they ever place, not their total spend.

hasDefinedTerm.name: LTV to CAC Ratio
hasDefinedTerm.description: How many rupees of lifetime contribution you get for every rupee spent acquiring the customer.

hasDefinedTerm.name: CAC Payback Period
hasDefinedTerm.description: How long it takes for a customer's cumulative contribution to repay what you spent acquiring them.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Repeat Purchase Rate
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of customers who buy again within a given period.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Purchase Cycle
hasDefinedTerm.description: The typical gap between one order and a customer's next. A supplement might be 30 days; a jacket, a year.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cohort
hasDefinedTerm.description: A group of customers who first bought in the same period, tracked together over time.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Churn
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of customers who stop buying over a given period.

hasDefinedTerm.name: RFM
hasDefinedTerm.description: Recency, Frequency, Monetary value: a way of segmenting customers by how recently they bought, how often, and how much they spend.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Direct to Consumer
hasDefinedTerm.description: Selling straight to the customer from your own store, rather than through a retailer or distributor.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Return to Origin
hasDefinedTerm.description: An order that ships out, fails to be delivered or is refused, and comes back to you. Overwhelmingly a cash-on-delivery problem.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Cash on Delivery
hasDefinedTerm.description: The customer pays the courier in cash when the parcel arrives, rather than paying online up front.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Prepaid Ratio
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of orders paid online before dispatch, as opposed to COD.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Payment Gateway Fee
hasDefinedTerm.description: The cut a payment processor takes on each online transaction, typically around 2% in India.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Marketplace Commission
hasDefinedTerm.description: The percentage Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa and similar platforms take from each sale.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Quick Commerce
hasDefinedTerm.description: Ten-to-thirty-minute delivery platforms: Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, Flipkart Minutes.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Fulfilment Cost
hasDefinedTerm.description: Everything it takes to get an order to the door: pick, pack, packaging materials and courier charges.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Contribution Margin 1
hasDefinedTerm.description: What's left of net revenue after the product itself: raw material, packaging, labour, inbound freight. The first rung of the ladder.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Contribution Margin 2
hasDefinedTerm.description: CM1 minus the cost of getting the order to the customer's door: shipping, payment gateway, packing and warehousing.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Contribution Margin 3
hasDefinedTerm.description: CM2 minus returns and the cost of acquiring the customer. The true per-order contribution: the only one that pays for salaries, rent and profit.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Fixed Overhead
hasDefinedTerm.description: Monthly costs that don't move with order volume: salaries, rent, software, retainers.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Break-even Units
hasDefinedTerm.description: The number of orders a month at which total contribution exactly covers fixed costs.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation & Amortisation
hasDefinedTerm.description: Operating profit before financing costs, tax and non-cash charges. A rough proxy for cash generated by the business itself.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Earnings Before Interest & Tax
hasDefinedTerm.description: EBITDA after depreciation and amortisation. Also called operating profit.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Profit After Tax
hasDefinedTerm.description: What the business actually keeps once everything: costs, depreciation and tax - is paid. Also called net profit.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Depreciation & Amortisation
hasDefinedTerm.description: The spread-out cost of assets you already paid for: moulds, machinery, tooling, software - charged a bit each month.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Maximum Retail Price
hasDefinedTerm.description: The printed price including GST: the number on the pack, before any discount.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Goods & Services Tax
hasDefinedTerm.description: Indian indirect tax included in the price the customer pays. It's collected on the government's behalf, never yours.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Month-on-Month Growth
hasDefinedTerm.description: How much a figure grew against the previous month.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Year-on-Year Growth
hasDefinedTerm.description: A period compared against the same period twelve months earlier.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Run Rate
hasDefinedTerm.description: The current month's revenue projected forward as if it held for twelve months.

mainEntity.name: What is a good ROAS for a D2C brand?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any figure above your break-even ROAS, which comes from your own cost sheet: COGS, shipping, payment fees and RTO rate. A 3x ROAS is excellent for one cost structure and loss-making for another.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between ROAS and MER?

acceptedAnswer.text: ROAS is revenue divided by ad spend, usually per platform and subject to attribution disputes. MER, or Marketing Efficiency Ratio, is total company revenue divided by total marketing spend, so it never has to assign credit to a channel.

mainEntity.name: Should LTV be calculated on revenue or contribution?

acceptedAnswer.text: Contribution. Lifetime revenue ignores COGS, shipping and fees, which badly flatters the number. LTV built on contribution tells you what is genuinely available to pay for acquisition.

mainEntity.name: What is RTO and why does it matter in India?

acceptedAnswer.text: RTO means return to origin: an order that ships, fails delivery or is refused, and comes back. It is largely a cash-on-delivery problem. A returned order earns nothing but still pays shipping in both directions, so a high RTO rate can move break-even ROAS by more than a full turn.
